taxonomic_note: Current Kew accepts C. pitcheri with var. pitcheri and var. dictyota. This learner remains species-level with local evidence centered on var. pitcheri.
look_here_first: Look for the nodding leathery urn: dull blue-purple to reddish-purple sepals stay connivent for most of their length, then develop narrow expanded, often crisped/recurved tips.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Travis — prior UT PRC herbarium voucher under Clematis pitcheri var. pitcheri; Uvalde — prior Harvard wild specimen from Nueces River; Kerr — Singhurst et al. (2010), Flora of Kerr Wildlife Management Area, vouchers JS 10559, JS 10823, LS 3861, p.518. These three counties meet the strict 24-county project threshold; old Williamson record is out-of-zone.
project_inclusion.range_audit_note: Prior PASS incorrectly treated Williamson as a target-zone county. Retain learner admission and actual Williamson observation as external-zone context, but demote PASS pending third approved-zone county evidence.

source_links.role: Kerr WMA natural flora vouchers JS 10559, JS 10823, LS 3861

native_range_reconciliation.note: Prior 2026-10-13 boundary correction downgraded an unsupported 3-county PASS. New independent Kerr specimen evidence fills the third target county. Species-level determination preserved; no infraspecific assignment.

best_field_traits: four thick leathery bluish to reddish-purple sepals
distal sepal margins narrowly expanded and often crispate/recurved
achene beaks short, about 1–3 cm, nearly glabrous to appressed-pubescent
morphology_keys.habit: Perennial woody-based climber, commonly dying back above ground.
morphology_keys.leaf_morphology: Simple to 1–2-pinnate; leaflets variable and often coarsely reticulate.
morphology_keys.flower: Nodding leathery purple urn with narrow expanded/crisped distal sepal margins.
morphology_keys.fruit: Achenes with relatively short 1–3 cm beaks, not strongly plumose.

comparisons.key_distinctions: C. texensis has true scarlet sepals with non-expanded non-crispate margins and longer plumose achene beaks. Older reticulata concepts require modern taxonomic caution.
